evidence.quoted_text:
/**
 * The CLI parses flag values as JSON when they parse, so an all-digit
 * cluster id (`--clusterId=12345678`) arrives as a NUMBER. Ids never start
 * with a zero that JSON would drop (JSON rejects leading zeros, so such ids
 * stay strings), which makes the integer form recoverable exactly — but only
 * when the number ALREADY has all eight digits. A shorter number is left as
 * a number and fails the regex rather than being zero-padded into some other
 * cluster's id.
 */
const ClusterIdInput = z.preprocess(
  (value) =>
    typeof value === 'number' &&
    Number.isSafeInteger(value) &&
    value >= 10_000_000 &&
    value <= 99_999_999
      ? String(value)
      : value,
  z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{8}$/, 'expected the 8-hex-digit cluster id from analyze.run'),
evidence.reason: The current `ClusterIdInput` still cannot recover ids that the CLI parses as exponent numbers. It only converts numeric values already in the range 10,000,000–99,999,999, so `12e45678` (Infinity) and `123456e7` (1,234,560,000,000) are still rejected. `0e123456` is now rejected instead of padded to `00000000`, but that only fixes the silent-misselection case; the raw text is still lost because the comment confirms the CLI JSON-parses flag values. Thus `analyze.fix --clusterId=<id>` still cannot select such clusters. The change does not implement the suggested raw-string preservation in the CLI.
